newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Several European bourses end at record highs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Several European bourses end at record highs.

text.p: Several European stock markets closed at record highs on Monday, propelled by the strong U.S. dollar.
The dollar lingered near a six-year peak against the mark despite dealers reporting Bank of Italy intervention to prop up the mark against a firm lira.

Single-European-currency jitters and expectations high German unemployment will continue to keep interest rates there low compared with other countries has kept the mark under pressure against most currencies.

Many economists predict that if the planned single currency, or euro, starts on time in 1999, it will be softer than the mark. That, coupled with perceptions British rates will rise further this year and the next step in U.S. rates will be higher, kept the mark depressed.
The Bank of England raised its base rate a quarter point last week, but most analysts predict more rate increases will be necessary to slow consumer demand and keep inflation tame.
Sterling surged early in the session above 3.03 marks, its the highest level since October 1990, and ended at 3.0237.
The dollar also gained against the mark after Austrian National Bank General Director Adolf Wala said he expected the dollar to reach 1.80 marks, compared with current levels just over 1.79.
The dollar's jump, coupled with a firm Wall Street start, pushed German, Finnish, Swedish and Dutch shares into record ground, while London shares surged to a record close on bid speculation.
A strong dollar generally makes European exports cheaper abroad and boosts exporters' profits.

"What we've seen (in German stocks) so far is perfectly justified with the dollar at this level," a Frankfurt dealer said when Germany's IBIS DAX index hurdled 4,100 points for the first time in pre-bourse, electronic trade.
The bourse-traded 30-share DAX index closed up more than two percent at a record high 4,124.19 points, just off its all-time intraday high of 4,127.97.
Leading German shares included dollar-sensitive drug, engineering and car stocks. Drugs group Schering AG ended up 3.20 marks at 198.50, off its year high of 199.40 set earlier.

In Helsinki, cellular phone maker Nokia Ab Oy and forestries shares benefited most from the higher dollar, brokers said. Nokia finished up 9.20 markka at 428.20, off its intraday high of 431.00, which was just a breath away from its all-time high 433.00 set last week.
Amsterdam stocks were also helped by positive half-year earnings expectations.
"To me, it's about enough, but everyone is positive on the (upcoming) half-year figures," a dealer said. "So, we're heading even higher. This strong dollar is ideal for dollar-sensitive stocks."

In Stockholm, traders said the Dow Jones Industrial Average's firmness gave stocks an added boost. At 1605 GMT, the Dow was up 22.06 points at 7,943.88 on expectations of positive second-quarter earnings reports.

In London, "I think it's down to takeover and bid speculation," said Gareth Evans, equities strategist at Nikko Europe. "The overall view hasn't changed, which is still one of caution because of sterling's strength."
Sterling's surge was seen squeezing British export firms' profits.

Chemicals giant Imperial Chemical Industries Plc closed at 882 pence, off its year high set earlier at 890, after the company said it would sell its polyester polymer, titanium dioxide and polyester film businesses to U.S. firm DuPont Co for $3 billion.
Paris markets were closed for the Bastille Day holiday.
CURRENCIES AT THE CLOSE
The dollar was little changed at 113.90 yen and 1.7935 marks versus 113.85 and 1.7705 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 57.9 points at 4,857.4, up 1.21 percent.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 83.22 points at 4,124.19.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 12.50 points at 2,941.59 on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
London gold closed at $320.85 per ounce, up 80 cents from Friday. Silver closed down 8 cents at $4.31.
